content_preview.title: JWST Detects Hidden Giant Planet in Beta Pictoris System Through Spectroscopy, Not Direct Imaging
content_preview.summary: Webb found Beta Pictoris d by reading its atmosphere's chemical fingerprint, a first for exoplanet discovery, while a separate imaging study independently confirmed it.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Astronomers using NASA's James Webb Space Telescope have found a giant planet hiding within one of the most intensely studied planetary systems in the galaxy, according to [NASA](https://science.nasa.gov/missions/webb/nasas-webb-discovers-hidden-planet-in-famous-star-system/). The new world, Beta Pictoris d, was not spotted as a point of light the way its two known siblings were. Instead, researchers detected the chemical fingerprint of its atmosphere buried inside spectroscopic dat...

recommendations: Added astrobiology.com to config/source_allowlist.txt (verified republication of NASA's own release, credited '[NASA]' inline).

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (1173 words) following the Overview/What We Know/What We Don't Know/Analysis format. Correctly separates the two independent discovery papers and their differing mass/semi-major-axis estimates, and flags the discrepancy explicitly in 'What We Don't Know' rather than glossing over it.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all four snapshots from disk (sources/2026-07/jwst-detects-hidden-giant-planet-in-beta-pictoris-system-through-spectroscopy-not-direct-imaging/): source-0.html.gz (science.nasa.gov, sha256 verified against manifest), source-1.html.gz (arXiv:2606.23789, Gibbs et al., 'Discovery of an Exterior Third Planet Orbiting Beta Pictoris', sha256 verified), source-2.html.gz (arXiv:2606.23801, Sutlieff/Bonse et al., 'Direct Imaging Discovery of Giant Exoplanet Beta Pictoris d', sha256 verified), source-3.html.gz (astrobiology.com, sha256 present). All manifest entries have status_code 200 and suspicious_patterns: null. astrobiology.com's article is a verbatim, credited republication of the NASA press release ('[NASA]' byline); content matches the NASA snapshot line for line where compared. All direct quotes attributed to NASA (Gibbs and Ruffio quotes, 'spread out like a barcode', 'A spectrum contains an incredible amount of information', 'the first directly imaged planet discovered primarily through moderate-resolution spectroscopy') are verbatim in source-0. All quoted fragments attributed to the two arXiv abstracts ('was serendipitously detected in JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations', 'the first planet discovered using spectral template matching with moderate-resolution spectroscopy', 'non-coronagraphic observations obtained with VLT/ERIS as well as multi-epoch archival datasets from JWST/NIRCam and VLT/SPHERE', 'highlights the deep sensitivity achievable with ground-based imaging in the mid-infrared and the discovery potential of future high-contrast observations with the Extremely Large Telescope') are verbatim in the respective abstracts. Numeric specifics (63 ly, 23 Myr, >30 au / 2-4 Jupiter masses from Gibbs et al.; 26.0 au, 89.0 deg inclination, 600 K, 2.4+/-0.6 Jupiter masses from Sutlieff/Bonse et al.) all trace exactly to the cited paper.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Cross-paper attribution independently verified against the raw abstract text, per the contributor's self-flagged concern: arXiv:2606.23789 (Gibbs, spectroscopy/discovery paper) abstract states 'The extracted spectrum shows clear CH4, CO, and H2O absorption features' -- confirming the article correctly attributes methane/carbon-monoxide/water absorption to the spectroscopy paper. arXiv:2606.23801 (Sutlieff/Bonse, direct-imaging confirmation paper) abstract states 'Its red F410M-F444W color indicates strong CO2 absorption in its atmosphere' -- confirming the article correctly attributes the distinct carbon-dioxide finding to the imaging paper, not the spectroscopy paper. No swap or cross-contamination found; the contributor's own re-verification was accurate. Also confirmed the contributor's chemical-formula-paraphrase choice: the article never places 'CO2', 'CH4', etc. inside quote marks -- it paraphrases as 'carbon dioxide', 'methane', 'carbon monoxide', 'water' in unquoted prose, avoiding any Unicode-subscript vs. plain-text quote mismatch with the LaTeX-formatted arXiv abstracts.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual throughout. The single regex hit on 'incredible' is inside a verbatim, correctly quoted Ruffio quote ('A spectrum contains an incredible amount of information,' Ruffio said) reproduced exactly from the NASA snapshot -- not bot editorializing. Confirmed via direct string match against source-0.html.gz; this is a false positive of the coarse sensationalism regex, not a tone problem.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ and src/content/article-meta/ for 'beta pictoris' -- zero existing hits. This is genuinely new topic coverage; no duplicate. Three other JWST/exoplanet-adjacent pieces published this month (Betelgeuse companion star, Omega Centauri black hole, GJ 3378b) cover unrelated targets/subjects, so no overlap.
concerns: astrobiology.com is not on config/source_allowlist.txt; investigated and added it below rather than treating it as a defect -- see recommendations.

The two discovery teams report different mass/semi-major-axis estimates for the same planet (2-4 Jupiter masses / >30 au vs. 2.4+/-0.6 Jupiter masses / 26.0 au); the article already surfaces this honestly in 'What We Don't Know' rather than picking one figure, so this is a strength, not a defect.
recommendations: None -- no corrections warranted. Both automated findings were investigated and are false positives (see tone_assessment and this note).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Both automated-review findings turned out, on manual verification, not to be actual editorial defects: astrobiology.com is a legitimate, credited republication of NASA's own release (now allowlisted), and the flagged 'incredible' is inside an accurate direct quote. The contributor bot's own self-flagged concern -- correctly attributing the CO2 absorption finding to the imaging paper rather than the spectroscopy paper -- was independently verified against the raw arXiv abstract text and confirmed accurate. No misattribution, no hallucinated quotes, no unsourced specifics found anywhere in the piece. APPROVE, no corrections record needed.
